newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mayne says Optus float timing unclear.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mayne says Optus float timing unclear.

text.p: Australian transport, security and healthcare group Mayne Nickless Ltd said on Friday it remained committed to selling its 24.9 percent stake in Optus Communications.
But Mayne said the need to integrate Optus Communications with pay television operator Optus Vision made the timing of the Optus float uncertain.

"Mayne Nickless Chairman Mark Rayner said that Mayne Nickless remained committed to the divestment of its Optus Communications shareholding, although the the need to integrate the Optus Vision business and resolve the structural issues surrounding Optus Vision makes the timing of a float uncertain," the company said.

Earlier, Optus Communications announced that chief executive Ziggy Switkowski had tendered his resignation and would be replaced by Peter Howell-Davies, a former chief executive of Mercury Communications, a unit of Cable & Wirless Plc.
Mayne said it welcomed the appointment of Howell-Davies.
"His experience in the Mercury Telecommunications business in the U.K. will be invaluable for Optus," Rayner said.
Rayner said in a statement the changes announced by Optus had Mayne's full support.
Cable and Wireless has a 24.5 percent stake in Optus, the same as that held by BellSouth Corp of the United States.
Mayne and Optus have said previously they wanted to float Optus by the end of 1997.
Mayne's shares closed up eight cents at A$7.58.
